The [[1976 Winter Olympics]], officially known as the XII Olympic Winter Games, was a winter [[multi-sport event]] held in [[Innsbruck]], [[Austria]], from 4 to 15 February 1976. A total of 1,123 athletes representing 37 [[National Olympic Committee]]s (NOC) participated in 37 events from 10 different [[Olympic sports|sports and disciplines]].<ref name="IOC">{{cite web |title=Innsbruck 1976 Winter Olympics |url=http://www.olympic.org/en/content/Olympic-Games/All-Past-Olympic-Games/Winter/Innsbruck-1976/ |work=Olympic.org |publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=1 August 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100813073149/http://www.olympic.org/en/content/Olympic-Games/All-Past-Olympic-Games/Winter/Innsbruck-1976/ |archive-date=13 August 2010 |url-status=live}}</ref> Two events were contested for the first time: the [[Figure skating at the 1976 Winter Olympics|figure skating]] discipline of [[ice dancing]], and the men's 1,000 metres in [[Speed skating at the 1976 Winter Olympics|speed skating]].<ref name="IOC" /><ref name="Ellensburg">{{cite news |last=Hughes |first=Mike |title=In Olympic 1,000 meter event – Mueller wins speed skating event |url=https://news.google.pt/newspapers?id=N8U0AAAAIBAJ&sjid=jI8DAAAAIBAJ&pg=5041,2121642&dq=speed+skating+1000+meters&hl=en |access-date=1 August 2010 |newspaper=[[Daily Record (Washington)|Daily Record]] |location=Ellensburg, Washington |date=12 February 1976 |page=6 |archive-date=29 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220329233825/https://news.google.pt/newspapers?id=N8U0AAAAIBAJ&sjid=jI8DAAAAIBAJ&pg=5041,2121642&dq=speed+skating+1000+meters&hl=en |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[File:1964 Winter Olympics USSR stamp.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Soviet stamp celebrating the awards of the Soviet athletes at the XII Winter Olympics]]
Sixteen NOCs won at least one medal, and twelve of them secured at least one gold. The [[Soviet Union at the 1976 Winter Olympics|Soviet Union]] clinched the first place in the gold and overall medal counts, with 13 and 27, respectively. Moreover, the Soviet team also collected the most silver (6) and bronze (8) medals. The host nation, [[Austria at the 1976 Winter Olympics|Austria]], concluded its participation with a total of six medals (two golds, two silvers, and two bronzes).<ref name="IOC" />
 
[[Liechtenstein at the 1976 Winter Olympics|Liechtenstein]] won its first Olympic medals: two bronzes by [[Willi Frommelt]] and [[Hanni Wenzel]] in the [[Alpine skiing at the 1976 Winter Olympics|alpine skiing]] slalom events.<ref name="liechtenstein">{{cite web |title=Sports Successes/Highlights |url=http://www.liechtenstein.li/en/eliechtenstein_main_sites/portal_fuerstentum_liechtenstein/fl-sport-sport/fl-sport-erfolge.htm |work=Portal Principality of Liechtenstein |publisher=Principality of Liechtenstein – Government Spokesperson's Office |access-date=2 August 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100911211741/http://www.liechtenstein.li/en/eliechtenstein_main_sites/portal_fuerstentum_liechtenstein/fl-sport-sport/fl-sport-erfolge.htm |archive-date=11 September 2010 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="Hanni Wenzel">{{cite news |title=For figure skating gold medal – Hamill appears unbeatable |url=https://news.google.pt/newspapers?id=NsU0AAAAIBAJ&sjid=jI8DAAAAIBAJ&pg=4441,2032529&dq=hanni+wenzel&hl=en |access-date=2 August 2010 |newspaper=[[Anchorage Daily News]] |date=12 February 1976 |agency=[[Associated Press]] |page=16 |archive-date=6 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306183649/https://news.google.pt/newspapers?id=NsU0AAAAIBAJ&sjid=jI8DAAAAIBAJ&pg=4441,2032529&dq=hanni+wenzel&hl=en |url-status=live }}</ref> [[East Germany at the 1976 Winter Olympics|East German]] athletes achieved gold medal sweeps in [[Luge at the 1976 Winter Olympics|luge]] and [[Bobsleigh at the 1976 Winter Olympics|bobsleigh]],<ref name="GDR">{{cite news |last=Tupper |first=Fred |title=Russian six takes title; U.S. medal bid fails; Russians win title; U.S. medal bid fails |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1976/02/15/archives/russian-six-takes-title-us-medal-bid-fails-russians-win-title-us.html |access-date=2 August 2010 |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |date=14 February 1976 |page=S1 |archive-date=22 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180722214654/https://www.nytimes.com/1976/02/15/archives/russian-six-takes-title-us-medal-bid-fails-russians-win-title-us.html |url-status=live }}</ref> which accounted for five of the country's seven Olympic titles. Alpine skier [[Rosi Mittermaier]] won the women's downhill and slalom events to give [[West Germany at the 1976 Winter Olympics|West Germany]]'s two gold medals in these Games. She came close to winning a third in the giant slalom, which would have made her the first woman to win all three Olympic alpine skiing events.<ref name="IOC" /><ref name="Rosi Mittermaier">{{cite news |title=Hamill captures gold; Rosi's sweep foiled |url=https://news.google.pt/newspapers?id=r8YRAAAAIBAJ&sjid=cO0DAAAAIBAJ&pg=6598,5091857&dq=rosi+mittermaier+first+woman&hl=en |access-date=2 August 2010 |newspaper=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |location=Spokane, Washington |date=14 February 1976 |agency=Associated Press |page=15 |archive-date=12 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231012233342/https://news.google.pt/newspapers?id=r8YRAAAAIBAJ&sjid=cO0DAAAAIBAJ&pg=6598%2C5091857&dq=rosi%20mittermaier%20first%20woman&hl=en |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Cross-country skiing at the 1976 Winter Olympics|Cross-country skier]] [[Helena Takalo]] contributed three of [[Finland at the 1976 Winter Olympics|Finland]]'s seven medals by reaching podium place finishes in all of the women's events.<ref name="Ellensburg" /> Two [[Netherlands at the 1976 Winter Olympics|Dutch]] speed skaters were responsible for five of their country's six medals: [[Piet Kleine]] won the men's 10,000 metres and came second in the 5,000 metres, while [[Hans van Helden]] secured bronze medals in the same events and also in the 1,500 metres.<ref>{{cite Sports-Reference |title=Speed skating at the 1976 Innsbruck Winter Games |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/1976/SSK/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417043021/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/1976/SSK/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=17 April 2020 |access-date=2 August 2010}}</ref> Before these Games, Great Britain's last Winter Olympic medal had been a gold at the [[1964 Winter Olympics|1964 Games]], also held in Innsbruck.<ref>{{cite Sports-Reference |title=Great Britain at the 1964 Innsbruck Winter Games |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/GBR/winter/1964/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417042749/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/GBR/winter/1964/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=17 April 2020 |access-date=2 August 2010}}</ref> Twelve years later in the same city, the [[Great Britain at the 1976 Winter Olympics|British]] team won again a single gold medal, this time by figure skater [[John Curry]] in the men's singles with a still-standing record total score.<ref name="IOC" /><ref name="John Curry">{{cite web |title=John Curry |url=http://en.beijing2008.cn/spirit/pastgames/halloffame/c/n214044807.shtml |work=The Official Website of the Beijing 2008 Olympic Games |publisher=The Beijing Organizing Committee for the Games of the XXIX Olympiad |access-date=2 August 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110623223756/http://en.beijing2008.cn/spirit/pastgames/halloffame/c/n214044807.shtml |archive-date=23 June 2011}}</ref> The two bronze medals won by [[Sweden at the 1976 Winter Olympics|Swedish]] athletes were not enough to prevent this team's performance from becoming the weakest ever in the nation's Winter Olympic history.<ref>{{cite Sports-Reference |title=Sweden |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/SWE/ |access-date=2 August 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100716034950/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/SWE/ |archive-date=16 July 2010 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

[[Andorra at the 1976 Winter Olympics|Andorra]] and [[San Marino at the 1976 Winter Olympics|San Marino]] sent their first delegations to the Winter Olympics,<ref name="San Marino">{{cite journal |title=San Marino and Olympism |journal=Olympic Review |date=January 1977 |issue=111 |pages=29 |url=http://www.la84foundation.org/OlympicInformationCenter/OlympicReview/1977/ore111/ore111m.pdf |access-date=3 August 2010 |publisher=International Olympic Committee |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100809135340/http://www.la84foundation.org/OlympicInformationCenter/OlympicReview/1977/ore111/ore111m.pdf |archive-date=9 August 2010 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Andorra">{{cite journal |title=Andorra and Olympism |journal=Olympic Review |date=August–September 1982 |issue=178 |url=http://www.la84foundation.org/OlympicInformationCenter/OlympicReview/1982/ore178/ORE178w.pdf |access-date=3 August 2010 |page=503 |publisher=International Olympic Committee |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100809013904/http://www.la84foundation.org/OlympicInformationCenter/OlympicReview/1982/ore178/ORE178w.pdf |archive-date=9 August 2010 |url-status=live}}</ref> whereas the [[Republic of China at the 1976 Winter Olympics|Republic of China]] competed for the second and last time before its return as [[Chinese Taipei at the 1984 Winter Olympics]]; none of these teams medalled.

{{see also|Olympic medal table}}
The medal table is based on information provided by the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) and is consistent with IOC convention in its published medal tables. The table uses the [[Olympic medal table]] sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won, where a nation is an entity represented by a [[National Olympic Committee]] (NOC). The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next, and then the number of bronze medals.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ostlere |first1=Lawrence |date=11 August 2024 |title=Olympic medal table: USA beat China to top spot at Paris 2024 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2580716.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812015233/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2594580.html |archive-date=12 August 2024 |access-date=12 August 2024 |work=[[The Independent]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Araton |first1=Harvey |date=18 August 2008 |title=A Medal Count That Adds Up To Little |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321004238/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |archive-date=21 March 2023 |access-date=25 July 2024 |work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [[List of IOC country codes|IOC country code]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Cons |first1=Roddy |date=10 August 2024 |title=What happens if two countries are tied in the Olympic medal table? Tiebreaker rules explained |url=https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811152350/https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |archive-date=August 11, 2024 |access-date=11 August 2024 |work=[[Diario AS]] |language=en-us}}</ref>

==Change by doping==
{{main|List of stripped Olympic medals}}
[[Galina Kulakova]] of the [[Soviet Union at the 1976 Winter Olympics|Soviet Union]] finished 3rd in the women's 5&nbsp;km ski event, but was disqualified due to a positive test for banned substance [[ephedrine]]. She claimed that this was a result of using the nasal spray that contained the substance. Both the [[International Ski Federation|FIS]] and the [[International Olympic Committee|IOC]] allowed her to compete in the 10&nbsp;km and the 4×5&nbsp;km relay.<ref name=sr>{{cite Sports-Reference|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ku/galina-kulakova-1.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110120175019/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ku/galina-kulakova-1.html|archive-date=20 January 2011|df=dmy-all}}</ref> This was the first stripped medal at the Winter Olympics.
